modules.Alpharhabdovirinae: The collapsed catch-all: roughly 38 single-segment genera in one module, so most of its 36 features are lineage-specific accessories that exist in only one genus. Its N and G collections were corrected in September 2026 after the cross-feature QC found 46 sigmavirus glycoproteins filed under N (BV-BRC calls them “outer coat protein”) and nine BEFV GNS proteins filed under G.
modules.Betarhabdovirinae: Single-segment plant viruses. Its core proteins are divergent enough between species that four features needed the clustering identity dropped to 0.4–0.5 before the profiles would cover their own collections.
modules.Dichorhavirus: Two segments, and the only module where every feature with sequences behind it is built.
modules.Novirhabdovirus: Complete apart from the two G mature peptides. The highest self-recall in the family at 99.7%.

gaps:
Every declared feature now has a profile. The lineage-specific accessories that previously had no collection — named only in the literature, absent from the BV-BRC dump under any product string the binning rules match — have been removed from the declaration rather than left standing as permanent gaps.

Separately, G_MAT and G_SP are coordinate operations on curated G rather than binning products, and both now work. G_MAT gives 505 columns at 1000+ bits. G_SP was previously abandoned on a measurement error: a 19-residue profile scored with psiblast against proteins carries composition-based statistics that halve it (22 bits, read as “impossible”), where the annotator’s actual tblastn against the genome gives 47. Rebuilt as ten per-cluster profiles — 39–46 bits median, 100% self-recall — because a signal-peptide profile does not transfer even between lyssaviruses. Rabies now yields the full tiling: G 3318–4892, SP 3318–3374, mature 3375–4889.
